scenarios.prompt:
Get an MM3 verdict for the request below and tell me the MM3 run id. Send it exactly as written first.

mak:
  goal: routes/login.ts is safe to ship
  depth: quick
  where: [routes/login.ts]
  ask:
    concerns:
      auth:
        pass: no
        1: Is the password compared in plain text?
        2: Is the user looked up by a value from the request?
        3: Does a failed login say which part was wrong?
      session:
        pass: no
        4: Is the session id predictable?
        5: Is the session kept after logout?
        6: Is the session id sent over plain http?
      leaks:
        pass: no
        7: Does the login error reveal whether the email exists?
        8: Is the raw database error sent back?
        9: Does the response include fields the caller never asked for?

scenarios.title: Recover when the request goes in the wrong field
scenarios.story: A developer hands their agent a ready MM3 request and says: "Send this request to the MM3 tool, and tell me the verdict and the run id." Agents sometimes put the request under a field of their own, and the tool takes it only in "stdin".
scenarios.success: The agent's request met the stop that says what the tool ignored and where the YAML goes, its very next MM3 call was accepted, and it reports a run id that really exists. A run where the mistake never happens is reported as not exercised, never as a pass.
scenarios.matters: Before 0.1.2 this mistake answered "request: empty", which blames the wrong thing and sends an agent in circles. The new stop has to be enough to fix it, in one call.
scenarios.setupNote: Nothing is set up before the agent starts; the request is in the prompt. The job cannot force the mistake: it hands the agent a ready request and no hint about the tool's fields, and some agents will use "stdin" at once. Such a run does not exercise the feature and is reported as not exercised (a red "stop met" box), not as a pass.
scenarios.goal: An agent that sends its request under a field the MM3 tool ignores is told what was ignored, fixes it in its next call and gets a verdict.

Here is a ready MM3 request. Send this request to the MM3 tool, and tell me the verdict and the MM3 run id.

mak:

  depth: quick
  where: [routes/login.ts]
  ask:
    concerns:
      auth:
        pass: no
        1: Is the password compared in plain text?
        2: Is the user looked up by a value from the request?
        3: Does a failed login say which part was wrong?
      session:
        pass: no
        4: Is the session id predictable?
        5: Is the session kept after logout?
        6: Is the session id sent over plain http?
      leaks:
        pass: no
        7: Does the login error reveal whether the email exists?
        8: Is the raw database error sent back?
        9: Does the response include fields the caller never asked for?
    decisions:
      severity:
        pass: [none, low]
        10:
          scale: How severe is the worst issue?
          levels: [none, low, medium, high, critical]
      route:
        pass: [ship]
        11:
          choice: Where should this go?
          options: [ship, fix, block]

scenarios.title: Pass the guidance to a helper
scenarios.story: A developer asks the lead agent: "Have one helper check routes/login.ts with MM3, and tell me the MM3 run id the helper got." The helper does not share the lead's instructions; whatever it knows about MM3 has to come from the lead.
scenarios.success: The lead's prompt to the helper carries the delegate card or tells the helper to fetch it with `mm3 agent delegate`, the helper makes its own MM3 request and gets a verdict, and the run id the lead reports really exists in the ledger.
scenarios.matters: Helpers do not inherit the plugin's guidance. `mm3 agent delegate` is the only way it reaches them, so if leads do not hand it over, helpers start blind or skip MM3.
scenarios.goal: A lead agent hands one helper the delegate card, and the helper uses MM3 and reports a run id the lead passes on.
scenarios.prompt: Have one helper agent check routes/login.ts for access-control problems with MM3, and tell me the MM3 run id the helper got.

checkpoints.text: The agent calls MM3 at all
The lead hands the work to the expected number of helpers
Every helper's prompt carries the `mm3 agent delegate` card, or tells the helper to fetch it (a pointer works: the helper's own first call gets the same card)
A helper (not the lead) made its own MM3 request and got a verdict
Every agent that works gets a verdict within the promised number of verb requests
Each helper's report cites an MM3 run id
The final answer states the MM3 run id
Every run id the final answer cites is in the ledger
After every MM3 stop, the agent's very next call is MM3 again (never a file read, a shell command or a hand-off)

Counted as a verb request: class, scan, drill, loop, view or replay. Calls to agent, template, help, probe or doctor are discovery, not attempts.
